title: Any Duplicates?
description:
Given an array `nums`, return `true` if any number appears more than once, and `false` if every number is different.

Example: for `nums = [1, 2, 3, 1]` return `true`, because 1 appears twice.
hints: Concept: a `HashSet` is a collection that remembers which values it has seen. `set.contains(x)` answers "have I seen x before?" instantly, and `set.add(x)` remembers x.

Approach: go through the numbers once. For each number, check whether you've seen it already. If yes, there's a duplicate. If not, remember it and move on. (Comparing every pair with two loops also works, it's just slower.)

Pseudocode:
  seen = empty set
  for each x in nums:
      if seen contains x: return true
      add x to seen
  return false

workedExample.title: Count Distinct Numbers
workedExample.description: Return how many different values are in `nums`. For `[4, 4, 2, 7, 2]` the answer is `3`.
workedExample.explanation:
A set ignores values it already has, so adding every number leaves exactly one copy of each distinct value.

For your problem, check `contains` before adding: if the set already has the number, you've found a repeat.

walkthrough.note: 1 is already in seen. That's a duplicate, so return true.

mistakes.hint: The repeated numbers aren't next to each other. Compare each number with everything you've seen before, not just its neighbour. A HashSet makes that easy.
